terra.problem: The passage says Israel increased the altars, not that they bought them.
The verse does not say that growth went into altars instead of digging wells.
The image of a rich vine building towers is confusing rather than funny.
The verse does not say the pillars received credit or all the attention.
Verse 1 says Israel increased the altars and made the pillars better, not that both were multiplied.
The passage does not state that making things bigger was Israel's plan. It says the altars increased and the pillars were made better.
Calling Hosea a prophet is a Bible fact not stated in this passage, so it needs a reference.
Calling the tribute a gift or present obscures what the passage says: the calf will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king.
The verse says Samaria will be carried off with her king; it does not say nobody stays behind.
Saying 'no joke here' comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
The passage does not say what Israel already knew or establish that this was not new information to them.
The claim that famine appears in other Bible stories needs a reference.
Calling Hosea a prophet is a Bible fact not stated in this passage, so it needs a reference.
The passage says Ephraim will be harnessed, but does not state that she will be given another job besides threshing.
The comparison is confusing: a crown is worn on the head, not normally placed on a neck.
The passage does not say what Hosea has in mind. It can simply say the verse does not mention flowers.
The passage does not place this scene at a particular point in the farm year.
The verse mentions other things too, including sowing righteousness, reaping loving devotion and breaking up unplowed ground.
The passage does not say Israel counted on its fortresses. It says they trusted in their own way and their multitude of mighty men.
